title: With Grateful Hearts with Joyful Tongues
description: With Grateful Hearts with Joyful Tongues in Tonic Solfa to MELITA, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: Andrew Kippis wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 848 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “National Praise and Prayer”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre, six lines (8.8.8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELITA; any other Long Metre, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: With grate-ful hearts with joy-ful tongues, To God we raise u-ni-ted songs; His power and mer-cy we pro-claim: Through ev-ery age, O, may we own Je-ho-vah here has fixed his throne, And tri-umph in his might-y name.

lines: With grateful hearts with joyful tongues,
To God we raise united songs;
His power and mercy we proclaim:
Through every age, O, may we own
Jehovah here has fixed his throne,
And triumph in his mighty name.
Long as the moon her course shall run,
Or men behold the circling sun,
Lord, in our land support thy reign;
Crown her just counsels with success,
With truth and peace her borders bless,
And all thy sacred rights maintain.

licence: Public domain: Andrew Kippis died in 1795.
credits: Words by Andrew Kippis (1725–1795), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to MELITA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
